_meta.purpose: API object -> table -> PK -> identifying columns -> encryption status -> validation approach -> feasibility. Input to the DBUtils rewrite.
_meta.server_version: Microsoft SQL Server 2019 (RTM-CU32-GDR) 15.0.4455.2, Developer Edition, Linux (Ubuntu 20.04.6 LTS)
_meta.encryption_model: Application-side AES, base64-encoded at rest. DETERMINISTIC: identical plaintext yields identical ciphertext across every column and table (static key, no per-row IV or salt). Confirmed by ss_port having only 59 distinct ciphertexts across 20,651 rows and one ciphertext appearing in 3 columns across 2 tables. No SQL Server TDE / Always Encrypted in use.
_meta.classification_caveat: Encrypted-vs-plaintext is INFERRED from value shape (base64 charset, length a multiple of 4, decoding to whole 16-byte AES blocks, low printable-byte fraction). SQL Server reports these columns as plain varchar and offers no catalog hint. Every verdict below carries the sampled value that produced it.
_meta.identity_query: SELECT @@VERSION, DB_NAME(), SUSER_SNAME(), (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM sys.tables)

lever_1_audit_log_plaintext.description: PRIMARY LEVER. sso_arcos_log records every business write with a PLAINTEXT object reference, so a created object can be matched by name even though the business table encrypts that same name.

key_columns.sal_id: bigint, PK, identity - use for cheap range scans
key_columns.sal_object_referance: varchar, PLAINTEXT - the object name, e.g. 'AUTO40PC47', '10.11.0.48@SVC40PC47:Windows RDP'
key_columns.aot_description: varchar, PLAINTEXT - object type, e.g. 'User Transactions', 'Service Transactions'
key_columns.sal_old_value: varchar - previous value, usable for UPDATE validation
key_columns.sal_new_value: varchar - new value, usable for UPDATE validation
key_columns.sal_ipaddress: varchar - caller IP; the test runner appeared as 10.10.1.242
key_columns.sal_Api_user_id: int - NON-NULL only for API-originated writes. The cleanest API-vs-UI discriminator

lever_1_audit_log_plaintext.caveat: OVER-REPORTS creation. 6 audit rows say 'Created / User Transactions / AUTO40PC47' but only 1 sso_users row exists. The audit log records the ATTEMPT, not the durable insert. Must always be paired with lever 2 or 3.

lever_2_ciphertext_equality.description: Because encryption is deterministic, an exact-match lookup on an encrypted column works WITHOUT decrypting - provided the test can obtain the ciphertext for the expected plaintext.
lever_2_ciphertext_equality.verified: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM sso_users WHERE ssu_username = 'OhjN7MeS4xe7sCksQFhyTMUAKRTy1ZbFzZu+2KUHDAk=' returned exactly 1
lever_2_ciphertext_equality.how_to_obtain_ciphertext: Two options: (a) read it back once from the row the API created and reuse it as a fixture; (b) reimplement the product's AES routine plus key in the framework - key material and algorithm live in the product source, NOT supplied here. Option (a) requires no key and is recommended.
lever_2_ciphertext_equality.limitation: Cannot construct the ciphertext for a NEW, never-before-inserted name without the key. So this lever validates 'the row I just created still exists', not 'a row with this arbitrary name exists'.

lever_3_created_by_discriminator.description: The API stamps a PLAINTEXT actor into created_by / *_created_by. Rows the API created are therefore findable with no decryption at all.
lever_3_created_by_discriminator.usage: Pair with a timestamp window to isolate the rows one test run created.

lever_4_row_count_delta.description: Capture COUNT(*) before and after the call. Immune to encryption entirely. Distinguishes a real insert from an 'Already Exists' no-op, which the HTTP response cannot.
lever_4_row_count_delta.caveat: Not safe under concurrency - this QA database has continuous background write activity (see db-observations DB-010, DB-001).

lever_5_api_request_log.description: ArconPamApiLog captures the API's own per-call logging, including application error codes and unhandled .NET exceptions that the HTTP envelope hides.
lever_5_api_request_log.caveat: Only a clustered PK on LogId; LoggedOnDate and ApplicationName are UNINDEXED, so any date-range predicate is a full scan of 41.9M rows. Always bound the query by a LogId range first.

objects.validation_approach: Name is encrypted, so match on sls_id returned by the API, or on sls_created_by='SYSTEM_API' plus a sls_created_on window, or via sso_arcos_log with the plaintext LOB name.
objects.caveat: No LOB create was observed in sso_arcos_log during the run window, so the exact aot_description value for a LOB create is NOT MEASURED - confirm it before relying on it. tblLOBDetail (the ADbridging LOB table) has 0 rows.

objects.validation_approach: Best channel: sso_arcos_log where sal_object_referance = '<username>' AND aot_description='User Transactions' AND aoo_object_operation='Created', paired with a COUNT on sso_users filtered by created_by='SYSTEM_API' and a created_on window to confirm the insert was durable.
objects.note: ssu_username and ssu_displayname held the IDENTICAL ciphertext on the run-created row, independently confirming deterministic encryption.

objects.validation_approach: Fully plaintext table - direct name match. SELECT COUNT(*) FROM sso_ApiUsers WHERE Username = ? AND CreatedOn >= ?. The simplest and most reliable object to validate in the whole schema.
objects.security_note: Password, UsersSecret and UsersKey are stored in CLEARTEXT. See db-observations DB-008.

objects.validation_approach: Every natural identifier is encrypted. Use sso_arcos_log with aot_description='Service Transactions' and the plaintext composite reference '<ip>@<user>:<type>', paired with ss_created_by='SYSTEM_API' plus a ss_created_on window.
NO encryption anywhere in this table. Direct plaintext name match: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM sso_Sgroup WHERE srv_group_name = ?. The ideal object for a first DB-validation pilot.
NO encryption anywhere in this table. Direct plaintext name match: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM sso_Ugroup WHERE usr_group_name = ?.
objects.data_quality_note: A sampled usr_group_name was the literal two-character string '""' - the API accepts junk names. Consistent with the brief's finding of 3 [Required] properties across ~6,738.

objects.validation_approach: Only ID-based validation is available. The four companion profile tables are all EMPTY, so access-control profile behaviour cannot be validated against this database at all.
objects.reason: Stalest table surveyed - not modified since 2026-06-11, nothing created during the run, and every related profile table has 0 rows. There is no data to assert against.

freshness.max_timestamp_observed: 2026-07-29 21:35:00 within the queried window; table is actively written

objects.validation_approach: This is the validation channel for every other object. Fully plaintext, carries old/new values, and sal_Api_user_id isolates API-originated writes from UI ones.

referential_integrity.finding: Referential integrity is enforced in the application, not the database. Orphan rows exist and are measurable.

measured_orphans.check: ssR_Users_Services rows whose service is missing from sso_services
sso_lobs_users rows whose user is missing from sso_users
sso_lobs_users rows whose LOB is missing from sso_lobs
sso_users rows with no matching sso_user_details row

measured_denormalization_drift.check: sso_lobs_users.lug_sls_name vs authoritative sso_lobs.sls_name for the same lug_sls_id

denormalized_duplicate_columns.note: These are copies of authoritative values in the parent tables. They can and do drift, which makes them a genuine consistency-validation target.

framework_wiring.warning: db_user=devops is a sysadmin login over 31 databases. An automated test suite must NOT use it. See the least_privilege_account spec in docs/analysis/C-database-validation.md section 6.
